subject: MSA + Order Form: Ownership mapping & feedback license coordination
messages:
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@brighttech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brighttech.com
Date: 2026-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines (output ownership & training)

Jordan / Grace —

Appreciate the quick demo yesterday. Our legal and product teams reviewed your MSA and the draft order form. Attached are our redlines (BrightTech_MSA_redlines_v1.docx) focused on three areas we need clarity on:

1) Output ownership: Section 3.2 in our redline seeks explicit assignment of customer output for customer-provided prompts and outputs generated by models that are trained on customer data.
2) Training & data use: We have a carveout request — we want a firm commitment that Redwood will not use our production requests or output to further train general models without explicit opt-in.
3) Feedback license: We want any feedback we provide (bug reports, examples) to be restricted to non-exclusive right to use for operational improvements and not for model retraining or productization unless separately agreed.

Can you confirm Redwood's positions on these points and share any suggested alternate language? If possible, we'd like to get legal folks on a 30-minute call early next week to resolve outstanding items.

Attachments: BrightTech_MSA_redlines_v1.docx; OrderForm_BrightTech_20260715.pdf

Thanks —
Tom Rivera
Head of Platform Partnerships
BrightTech

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA + Order Form redlines (output ownership & training)

Folks — forwarding BrightTech's redlines (below). Quick read and proposed approach:

Summary of their asks (from Tom):
- Customer wants assignment of output generated from customer inputs and any models trained on their data.
- Explicit prohibition on using production requests/outputs for training without opt-in.
- Narrow feedback license only for operational improvements, not for retraining/productization.

My suggested positions (talking points for call):
- Output: We keep our standard approach — customer has broad rights to use outputs for their business, but we cannot assign model IP. Propose language: customer-owned output (for their inputs) + no assignment of Redwood model weights or derivatives.
- Training: Commit to not using customer production data to train our public models without explicit opt-in. Offer an auditable process (SLA/attestation + engineering isolation) and a contractual clause requiring opt-in for training.
- Feedback license: Accept a narrow, non-exclusive, royalty-free license limited to debugging, product improvement, and safety work that expressly excludes training for public models unless a separate commercial agreement is signed.

Action items I propose now:
- Laura: can you draft the suggested redline text for 3.2 (output) + training opt-out clause and put in Drive link by EOD?
- Ben: prepare a short engineers' note describing how we isolate and prevent production data from entering training pipelines (one pager we can share with BrightTech legal).
- Grace: join the call with legal and help steer where to make commercial concessions (pricing/credits if they require opt-in).

I also recommend we offer a short procurement-friendly SOW appendix that preserves productization rights for BrightTech on outputs they own, while protecting Redwood model IP.

I'll reply to Tom to propose Wed 11am PT for a legal-only call and attach our proposed redline.

Thanks —
Jordan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Mills <sara.mills@brighttech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@brighttech.com>, procurement@brighttech.com
Date: 2026-07-18T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (output ownership & training)

Jordan / Grace —

Thanks for the quick reply and for proposing language. I circulated Redwood's high-level positions to our counsel — see attached inline spreadsheet (BrightTech_inline_comments.xlsx) with our comments and a couple of asks that we couldn't resolve internally: 

1) Assignment request: our product team insists on assignment language for outputs generated from our proprietary prompts and datasets — they see this as necessary for downstream productization. If Redwood won't assign model IP, would you consider a limited assignment for those outputs plus a covenant not to exploit those outputs for your own commercial models?

2) Training opt-out: BrightTech needs contractual proof points (not just an engineering note). Can Redwood include a clause that (a) prohibits using our production requests/outputs for training public models, and (b) provides for audit rights or a quarterly attestation?

3) Feedback license: we like the proposed narrow license but need explicit carveouts that prevent feedback being fed into any model retraining pipeline without a separate commercial agreement. Also asking for a 12-month sunset on feedback rights in the absence of a follow-on agreement.

We think these can be resolved with clearer language and a short appendix that: (i) maps output categories to ownership (customer-owned outputs for customer inputs; derived model improvements remain Redwood IP), (ii) sets opt-in mechanics for training, and (iii) limits feedback license scope and duration.

Can we schedule a 30 minute legal-to-legal call tomorrow (Tue) at 11am PT or Wed at 11am PT? If Redwood can share the draft redline before the call, we can mark up quickly.

Best —
Sara Mills
Senior Counsel, BrightTech

Attachments: BrightTech_inline_comments.xlsx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@brighttech.com>, Sara Mills <sara.mills@brighttech.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (output ownership & training) — proposed redline and next steps

Tom / Sara —

Thanks for the detailed notes and the inline comments. Laura attached a first-pass redline that reflects our positions:
- Output: explicit customer rights to outputs generated from customer inputs; language that stops short of assignment of Redwood model weights or derivatives. Text includes an exportable "customer output" definition and a covenant that Redwood will not claim ownership over customer-generated outputs.
- Training: we will include a clause prohibiting the use of BrightTech production requests/outputs for training Redwood public models without explicit, documented opt-in. For operational improvements (latency, bug fixes, safety), we propose a non-training, aggregated telemetry clause and quarterly attestation.
- Feedback license: we accept a narrow, non-exclusive license limited to debugging and product safety that contains an express exclusion of retraining/public model productization; we can agree to a 12-month sunset on the license where reasonable.

Laura: attached file is "Redwood_proposed_redline_BT_v1.docx" (I'll upload to the Drive folder and send link after this). Ben: please prep the engineering attestation note so we can attach it to the redline for legal review.

Tom / Sara — can you confirm Wed 11am PT works for a 30 minute legal call? If so I'll send a calendar invite and the Drive link to the proposed redline.

Regards —
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_proposed_redline_BT_v1.docx

--
Jordan Blake
Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0134
